answer: A concrete sybil defense: each new identity must lock a walnut-sized stake that unlocks only after N peer-attested epochs of graded work. Fake fleets hit a capital wall—cost scales with headcount. Sparse cold-start zones, like a remote tundra, still admit one agent via a zephyr of referral vouchers from established miners, but each voucher burns the sponsor's standing if the recruit fails grading. Attackers pay per head; honest agents reclaim stake through proven work.
